notes: Q05.1: the documented upper bound of foot movement is the urgent double quick, 180 steps a minute of 33 inches (drill-timing.json double_quick_urgent, Hardee para 114; the step is inferred, the cadence documented); the 165-step double quick (2.305 m/s) is the lower end of the double-quick range. Horses: the manuals give point speeds for walk, trot and gallop, so only an upper bound exists; the slowest documented gallop of the three bases is the bound (the sources conflict: each is a selectable basis)

Q05.3: the turn of a formation is the stage's rigid rotation about the unit's origin; the far end of a column moves perpendicular to the unit's advance, so its speed is sqrt(v^2 + (omega r)^2) with omega the peak rate of the smoothstep turn (1.5 x angle / turn time); the sum v + omega r is carried in the evidence
owed: Q05.4: an open register entry, with the dated search log of GATE-SPEC 1.4, that records the offsets of the layer (report().offsets, defects and state_offsets: a documented time that the documented rate cannot meet), so that the lateness items can be COVERED instead of BLOCKED-INPUT

Q05.5: a documented rate of movement for limbers, caissons, wagons and the forge, gun pieces on the road and a cavalry column (the Instruction for Field Artillery 1863 and Wheeler 1863 give horse speeds, not vehicle or column rates) and an open L3 register entry with a dated search log for each class (GATE-SPEC 1.4)
